title: nightshift-gpu-heap-corruption-notes
content:
Context
------
Night shift (2026-07-14 01:30-03:40 UTC) we observed a cluster of GPU node daemon panics on the eu-west-1 infer pool. Symptoms across 3 physical hosts: repeated kernel oops, nvidia module backtraces, and an eventual full kernel panic forcing an automatic reboot. ECC correctable error counters were rising on the affected devices prior to the crash; NVLink topology messages show intermittent link resets immediately before the first oops on two hosts.

Why this doc
--------
Quick, informal record of the nightshift triage: raw observations, hypotheses we discussed, short commands/scripts we used, and an actionable follow-up plan. Not a final postmortem — that will be a separate doc once root cause narrows. This is intentionally rough so future oncalls can pick up where we left off.

What we saw (timeline notes)
---------------------------
- 01:27 UTC: Pager alerts start for node infer-eu-1a-gpu-214 (OOM and kernel panic).
- 01:28 UTC: SRE oncall (Marisol) ssh to host; dmesg shows repeated lines: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid 11423, ..." and "nvidia: GPU 0: ECC single-bit error detected (correctable)". Soft ECC counters incrementing.
- 01:33 UTC: NVLink messages in dmesg: "nvlink: link down on device 0000:65:00, reset pending" then "nvlink: link up". Those map to physical GPUs connected by NVLink on board B.
- 01:40 UTC: Second host (infer-eu-1b-gpu-98) starts showing inconsistent dma mapping warnings in kernel logs; nvidia module backtrace present; we triggered a safe reboot.
- 02:10 UTC: Third host shows kernel oops with call trace referencing nvidia.ko and then a general protection fault in kernel leading to panic. Reboot loop briefly.
- 02:45 UTC: We put the three hosts into maintenance and drained pods; alerts quieted.
- 03:20 UTC: Quick stress test run on one host (cpu+mem stress + small CUDA workload) did not immediately reproduce after cold boot, but ECC counters start creeping up within 20–30s under CUDA microbench.

Immediate data captured
----------------------
- dmesg excerpts (saved to /var/log/sre/nightshift/gpu-2026-07-14/). Key lines we copied into the incident folder: 
  - "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79"
  - "nvlink: link down on device 0000:65:00"
  - "[Hardware Error]: Corrected ECC on GPU 0: count=23"
  - kernel oops call traces (nvidia+kmalloc context)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,utilization.gpu,ecc.mode.supported,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv -l 2 (periodic capture)
- journalctl -k -b -1 saved for each affected host.
- stack traces captured by crash scripts (sre-crashdump) and uploaded to central S3 for later analysis.

Hypotheses discussed
--------------------
1) NVLink transient resets are causing driver state corruption when combined with heavy allocation churn. Evidence: link down/up messages immediately before oops, affected GPUs are NVLinked pairs.
2) A recent kernel/dkms combo (linux-6.4.12 + nvidia-535.54) introduced an edge-case in the driver's error path, causing an invalid free (heap corruption) when handling ECC callbacks. Evidence: we upgraded kernel images on these hosts in the past 3 days, and the same driver version rolled out 5 days ago.
3) Hardware degradation (memory/VRAM faults) on a single GPU causing cascading ECC floods that stress driver recovery code. Evidence: ECC counts sporadically high on GPU0 on all three hosts.
4) Workload pattern (small repeated ephemeral allocations from our microbatching agents) creates pathological allocation/free pattern that exposes a latent driver bug. Evidence: stress microbench reproduces ECC increase quickly post-boot under the same workload.

Quick triage commands and what we looked for
------------------------------------------
- dmesg | egrep -i "nvlink|NVRM|ecc|oops|panic"
- sudo nvidia-smi -q | egrep -i "Ecc|Pending|Link" -A4
- journalctl -u kubelet -b --since "01:00" — to correlate pods starting/stopping around the event
- lsmod | grep nvidia; modinfo nvidia | sed -n '1,10p'
- /opt/sre/snapshots/gpu-oom-watch.sh to capture running processes and GPU memory maps
- echo 1 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/nvlink_disable (note: this is not a documented/prod knob; tested in a lab host only)

Short-term mitigations we tried (and why)
----------------------------------------
- Drained and rebooted the 3 hosts to break the immediate crash loop. Effective.
- Isolated pods running heavy ephemeral allocation workloads and rescheduled to other pools to reduce reproduction while we triage.
- Rolled back a non-critical kernel update on one host to see if stability improved (partial: host stayed up, but not a conclusive A/B). We did not roll back cluster-wide because we lacked statistical confidence.
- Temporary removal of NVLink via BIOS on one lab board (hardware lab) prevented the link-reset messages and the microbench did not cause an immediate ECC surge — suggests NVLink involvement but not definitive.

Why this is different from previous incidents
-------------------------------------------
- Previous ECC spikes were single-host and resolved by GPU reset; this event had NVLink link flaps ahead of driver oops and multiple hosts affected in a short window.
- Pattern points to interaction of NVLink topology + recent kernel/driver changes + allocation pattern. We haven't seen this triad in prior postmortems.

Open questions (to answer in the follow-up postmortem)
----------------------------------------------------
- Are all affected hosts running the exact same kernel and nvidia driver builds? (Inventory audit pending)
- Is there a firmware/board revision correlation across the three hosts? (I/O tagged on asset inventory)
- Does disabling NVLink at the OS driver level (or physically) eliminate crashes in production-like stress? (lab test scheduled)
- Can we reproduce the call trace locally with a minimized test-case (small C++ CUDA app that alloc/free loops while hammering NVLink traffic)?

Planned follow-ups (owners + ETA)
--------------------------------
- Inventory & correlation (Hannah) — confirm kernel/driver/firmware across affected hosts. ETA 2026-07-16.
- Repro test harness (Amit) — build a small workload that allocs/frees + NVLink transfers to try to reproduce the exact oops within lab. ETA 2026-07-18.
- Driver bisect plan (Connor) — identify candidate driver/kernel combos to A/B test in isolated pool (use cluster-managed lab nodes). ETA 2026-07-21.
- Temporary policy: autoscale rule to avoid scheduling microbatcher pods on machines with NVLink until we have a fix (Marisol to implement today).

Runbook draft notes (what we would add/change)
---------------------------------------------
- Add a quick triage checklist for NVLink-related panics: dmesg search patterns, nvidia-smi nvlink status, ECC counter snapshot, kernel oops signature match list.
- Add guidance for safe node isolation: drain -> capture crashdump -> cold reboot -> monitor ECC for 30 minutes under controlled workload before returning to rotation.
- Add a section on evidence collection to S3: exact dmesg, modinfo, nvidia-smi snapshots, last 10 lines of kernel logs.
- Consider a proactive probe job that samples ECC counters across the fleet hourly and alerts when rate > threshold in a short window.

Notes-to-self / informal ideas
-----------------------------
- If driver code is corrupting heap during error recovery, valgrind is useless for kernel modules; need kernel debug builds and KASAN or kgdb attached. Arrange debug kernel boots in lab.
- Could try a quick test: load driver module with nvlink intentionally blacklisted on one lab node, reproduce microbench. If stable, this narrows to NVLink path.
- Ask infra-provisioning to tag the 3 hosts as "nvlink-triage-2026-07". Makes log queries easier.

Immediate action items logged
---------------------------
- [x] Drain & reboot affected hosts (Marisol) — completed 2026-07-14 03:15 UTC.
- [ ] Inventory table (Hannah) — in progress.
- [ ] Repro harness in lab (Amit) — scheduled.
- [ ] Driver/kernel bisect plan (Connor) — draft in GH linked above.

If you read this in the morning: thanks to the night team for the quick isolation. Please add any missing logs or pointer snippets to the S3 bucket: s3://redwood-infra/sre/gpu-triage/2026-07-14/ and annotate this doc. We'll convert to a formal incident report when we have a repro or driver-level confirmation.

-- Marisol
